**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The degree-one block.** For $I=\{0\}$, level $2$ and charge $(0,0)$ the degree-one cyclotomic quotient is $H^{(0,0)}_1=\mathbb C[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ by the level-two instance of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], and it is already supported, so $B=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ with $x=x_1$. 2.1 **The symmetric form on $B$ and self-duality.** The coefficient functional $\tau(a+bx)=b$ is a symmetrizing trace on $B$: it is linear, $\tau(uv)=\tau(vu)$ for all $u,v$ (both sides pick out the $x$-coefficient of the product), and its radical is zero because $\tau(x)\ne0$, so the associated form $\langle u,v\rangle=\tau(uv)$ has matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in the basis $(1,x)$, which is nonsingular. This is the actual symmetric-algebra proof of cover self-duality, not an inference from self-duality of the head. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.2 **The degree-two block and its simple.** With $x=x_1$, $y=x_2$, $u=s_1$ the relations give $u^2=1$, $[x,y]=0$, $ux=yu-1$, $uy=xu+1$, $x^2=0$, and from $ux^2=0$ one gets $y^2=(x+y)u$, so the eight words $1,x,y,xy,u,xu,yu,xyu$ span the degree-two algebra; the models $(N,-N,-J)$ on $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with $N=E_{12}$ and $J$ the swap matrix, $(\epsilon,1+\epsilon,1)$ and $(\epsilon,-1+\epsilon,-1)$ on $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ satisfy all relations, and the central Hermite projectors of the element $z=x+y$ separate the three factors, which proves that the span of the eight words is isomorphic to $M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus B_+\oplus B_-$ with $B_\pm=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$. Since $s_2$ commutes with $x_1$, it commutes with $x_2$, and the recursion gives $x_3=x_2+s_2$. On either $s_2$ eigenspace this is $x_2\pm1$, which is invertible, contradicting nilpotence of $x_3$ at residue zero. Thus such a nonzero module cannot exist; applying this to the regular module proves the supported algebra is zero in every degree at least three. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

Induction from degree $0$ to the degree-one block gives the regular module of $B$; the supported induction from $B$ to the degree-two block $M_2(\mathbb C)$ sends the simple $\mathbb C$ to $\mathbb C^2$ and the regular module $B$ to $M_2(\mathbb C)$, which is two copies of the simple $\mathbb C^2$; explicitly $M_2\otimes_B\mathbb C=M_2/M_2N$ has dimension two and is the unique matrix-factor simple, whereas $M_2\otimes_B B=M_2$; restriction of $\mathbb C^2$ to $B$ is the regular Jordan module $B$ itself (the generator $x$ of $B$ acts on $\mathbb C^2$ as $N$ with $N^2=0$ and $\dim\ker N=1$), and restriction of $D_{01}=\mathbb C$ to degree zero is the one-dimensional $\mathbb C$-module.
